CHIEF COMPLAINT
Hypogonadism

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
59-year-old HIV-positive male on testosterone replacement therapy presenting for follow-up. Patient reports feeling vigorous with improved sleep. He notes positive effects from testosterone therapy with improvements in bloodwork. He continues finasteride 5mg at half-pill dosing and cialis at variable doses (5mg on workout days, 2.5mg on other days; currently out of supply). Patient inquired about indole-3-carbinol or broccoli extract for estrogen control. Patient requested increasing testosterone from current 140mg to 175mg. Doctor explained that patient's testosterone levels have previously peaked above 1,500, which increases risk of blood thickness and potential cardiovascular complications. Doctor advised against dose increase at this time, noting patient is doing well and does not require escalation. Patient agreed with this recommendation.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports good sleep quality and feeling vigorous. No other systems reviewed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
HIV positive

MEDICATIONS
- Testosterone 1 mL every 10 days (140mg)
- Finasteride 5mg, half-pill daily
- Cialis 5mg on workout days, 2.5mg on other days (out of supply)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient exercises regularly. Uses medication calendar for tracking testosterone injections. Pharmacy: Walmart. Prefers paper prescriptions.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Patient appears trim.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs noted.
Pulmonary: Lungs clear to auscultation, no concerns.

RESULTS
Triglycerides: 145 mg/dL (previous 265 mg/dL)
Cholesterol: Improved
Red blood cell count: Increased, stable
Estradiol: Not elevated
Testosterone: Previous peak >1,500 ng/mL
PSA: 0.6 (previous 0.5; normal <4 ng/mL)

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Hypogonadism on testosterone replacement therapy: Continue current dose of 1 mL (140mg) every 10 days. Declined dose escalation to 175mg due to risk of testosterone peaks >1,500 and associated blood thickness concerns.
2. Lipid panel: Continue to monitor; showing significant improvement on current testosterone therapy.
3. PSA: Stable and normal. Continue annual monitoring.
4. Estradiol: Not currently elevated. Recheck in fall if patient desires, though not necessary at this time.
5. Medications: Refill finasteride 5mg and cialis 5mg/2.5mg. Provide paper prescriptions to be filled at Walmart pharmacy.
